# docs_audit_report — 2026-06-27

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
The hero earns the scroll — "catch the reasoning errors your LLM states with
total confidence" plus the concrete 47+28=76 example is genuinely clear, and
`pip install carnot-ebm` is right there. But the moment a stranger scrolls into
the evidence, they hit a wall of unglossed benchmark acronyms, three different
HumanEval numbers, several suspiciously perfect scores, and a license that says
MIT-0 at the top and Apache 2.0 at the bottom. Net: strong open, trust-eroding
middle and footer. A careful evaluator closes the tab at the license line.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. LICENSE CONTRADICTION — hero badge + `<meta>` say "MIT-0"; the footer says
   "Apache 2.0 License." A stranger evaluating adoption cannot tell what the
   license actually is. This is the single most credibility-damaging defect.
2. EVIDENCE = JARGON WALL — the 12-card "What we measured" grid is acronym soup
   (FoVer, CCTU, SVAMP, VeriCoT, CRANE, PRM-BiasBench, HalluGuard v3, Ising)
   with THREE conflicting HumanEval deltas (+3.0 / +18pp / +15pp). A stranger
   can't tell which is THE result, so they trust none.
3. HEADLINE NUMBER IS UNEXPLAINED AND SELF-CONTRADICTORY — "0.9131 FoVer AUROC"
   headlines the hero, but a results card cites "0.125 FoVer baseline" (an AUC
   *below* random chance), and the first card a stranger sees stuffs in "5-seed
   dual-condition; architecture-only 0.8947; Repinned from v2 0.9857" — internal
   methodology baseball, not landing-page copy.

## DETAILED FINDINGS

### Bloat
- No single bento card exceeds the 120-word cap and no result card clearly
  exceeds 60 words — raw word-count bloat is NOT the main problem here. The
  bloat is structural/density, below:
- "Recent progress" r-card (hero stats bar, line 312) — ~50 words — under the
  60-word cap, but it is jammed *inside* `.stats-bar` (a flex row sized for
  4 tiny stat blocks). It will render squished/misplaced next to the numbers,
  and it carries methodology jargon into the first thing a stranger reads. Move
  it out of the stats bar; cut to one plain sentence.
- "What we measured" results grid — 12 cards — under the 20-card cap, but at
  this jargon density 12 is already "skim none." Recommend ≤6 headline cards,
  each with a one-line plain-English gloss.
- Nav bar — 11 text links + 2 buttons (13 items) — overwhelming for a landing
  page. Recommend ≤5 (Get Started, Results, Paper, GitHub, HuggingFace).

### Internal jargon
- Hero stat (line 308) — "FoVer math step-errors", "AUROC", "(5-seed)" — a
  conference stranger does not know what FoVer is or why 5 seeds matters. AUROC
  is borderline-acceptable for an ML audience but FoVer needs a one-line gloss
  ("FoVer: a public math step-error benchmark").
- "Recent progress" card (line 312) — "5-seed dual-condition", "architecture-only
  0.8947", "Repinned from v2 0.9857", "pre-submission adversarial audit" —
  pure insider methodology versioning.
- Typed-constraints + results cards — "CCTU constrained tool-use micro-benchmark"
  — CCTU never expanded; appears twice.
- TTC & PREM capability card — "scales Test-Time Compute (TTC) based on
  Process-Reward Energy Model (PREM) variance … intrinsic motivation for
  continuous self-learning" — the worst single card. Even with the inline
  expansions it is meaningless to a stranger and the last clause is hand-wavy.
- Results grid — "EstimationVerifier SVAMP AUC", "VeriCoT equation-style CoT
  fix", "GSM8K extraction TP rate", "CRANE vs rigid grammar", "PRM-BiasBench-style
  attacks", "k=5 ensemble", "HalluGuard v3", "0.0pp accuracy delta",
  "Ising-guided fuzzing" — SVAMP, VeriCoT, CoT, GSM8K, TP rate, CRANE, PRM,
  Ising are all unglossed; "0.0pp delta" and "k=5" are flag/jargon syntax.
- Preprint section — "position paper (paper-v6)" — "paper-v6" is internal
  versioning; a stranger doesn't care it's the 6th draft.
- API card — "VerdictRecord", "SessionMemory", "MCP server" — code-object names
  and an unexpanded acronym (Model Context Protocol).

### Per-milestone narrative
- The page mostly AVOIDS raw ".120 archived…" milestone narrative — good. But:
- Hero stat "382 Completed milestones" (line 306) — exposes internal project
  cadence; a stranger has no idea whether 382 is good, or what a "milestone" is.
- "Recent progress" card "Repinned from v2 0.9857 after pre-submission
  adversarial audit" — reads like a changelog entry, not landing copy.

### Inconsistencies
- LICENSE: "MIT-0" (line 7 meta, line 291 hero badge) vs "Apache 2.0 License"
  (line 766 footer). Direct contradiction.
- FoVer number: "0.9131 … AUROC on FoVer" (headline, line 308/312) vs
  "0.125 FoVer baseline" (line 550). FoVer is presented as both the flagship
  result and a near-zero baseline with no explanation tying them together.
- Metric naming: hero uses "AUROC"; results cards use "AUC" (SVAMP 0.90 AUC,
  prompt-injection "0.91 AUROC"). Mixed terminology for what reads as the same
  metric.
- HumanEval delta: "+3.0 points" (Code card + results), "66% → 84% (+18pp)"
  (Ising-guided fuzzing), "70% → 85% (+15pp)" (CRANE). Three different HumanEval
  results with no indication which is canonical.
- Two near-identical AUROCs: "0.9131" (FoVer math) and "0.91 (prompt-injection
  publication gate)" sit close enough to blur into one another.

### Missing essentials
- LICENSE — effectively missing because it is self-contradictory (MIT-0 vs
  Apache 2.0). A stranger cannot determine the real license.
- WHO MAINTAINS IT — only a footer copyright "© 2026 Ian Blenke." No "maintained
  by / team / contact" framing; reads as a solo project with no signal of
  continuity.
- WHY TRUST THE NUMBERS — the strongest trust anchor (FoVer independently
  re-computed on a clean CI checkout) is buried in the Preprint section, not
  near the headline number where a skeptic needs it.

### Fabrication signals
- "0.90 AUC (vs 0.125 FoVer baseline)" (line 550) — STRONGEST signal: an AUC of
  0.125 is far below 0.5 (worse than random / anti-correlated). Either a
  misreported number or a degenerate cherry-picked baseline; presenting
  "0.90 vs 0.125" as a win looks misleading.
- "GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0" — perfect 1.0.
- "k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks" — 100% on a small (60) sample, no anchor.
- "639 experiments … Zero false positives" (Dogfooding blog card) — perfect 0 FP.
- "2.0× speedup, identical losses" — "identical" is an unusually strong claim.
- "99.3% of wrong code flagged" — very high; plausible on 164 problems but no CI.

## WHAT'S WORKING
- The hero is excellent: one-sentence "what it does," the concrete 47+28=76
  example, and the install command are exactly what a stranger needs in 30s.
- The "Extract → Check → Repair" how-it-works section is plain-English and
  genuinely readable — it explains "energy" without requiring an EBM background.

## RECOMMENDED OPERATOR ACTIONS
1. Fix the license immediately — make the footer match the hero (MIT-0), or vice
   versa. This is the highest-priority single edit.
2. Resolve the FoVer 0.9131-vs-0.125 contradiction: drop the "0.125 baseline"
   card or explain in one clause why the same benchmark shows both numbers.
3. Rewrite the hero "Recent progress" card to one plain sentence; strip
   "5-seed dual-condition / architecture-only 0.8947 / Repinned from v2 0.9857"
   and move it out of the stats-bar `<div>` so it stops rendering squished.
4. Gloss or cut every benchmark acronym in the results grid (FoVer, CCTU, SVAMP,
   VeriCoT, CRANE, GSM8K, PRM-BiasBench, HalluGuard v3, Ising); trim the grid to
   ≤6 headline cards and pick ONE canonical HumanEval number.
5. Delete or fully rewrite the "TTC & PREM" capability card — it is unreadable
   to a stranger and inflates the "seven capabilities" count with internal
   plumbing (same for "Research operations," which describes how Carnot is built,
   not what a user can check).
6. Replace the "382 Completed milestones" stat with something a stranger can
   judge (e.g., supported models, or downloads); add a maintainer/contact line
   to the footer.
7. Surface the "independently reproduced on a clean CI checkout" trust anchor
   next to the headline 0.9131, not only in the Preprint section.
8. Preview the rendered page — stray `</div>` tags after several grids and the
   r-card nested in `.stats-bar` risk visible layout breakage.
